correctness.rationale: The proof derives the exact rank-one radius, reduces any nonzero square-zero factor to a norm-matched rank-one nilpotent for each test vector, and applies a positive spectral polynomial inequality. Approximate extreme spectral vectors establish optimality when endpoints are not eigenvalues. Strict concavity proves uniqueness, and endpoint asymptotics and attainment are checked. The bundled deterministic numerical checker passed 9,000 tests but is not used as an infinite proof.

General 2021 estimates do not determine this optimization.

originality.rationale: The 2022 universal sharp positive-product bound has no nonzero-spectral-minimum dependence, and the 2008 square-zero result assumes commuting factors with the square-zero factor first. The exact best curve for all noncommuting square-zero second factors, fixed positive A, arbitrary Hilbert dimension, and endpoint attainment are not implied by either. Searches for synonymous spectral-band, condition-number, quadratic/nilpotent and numerical-radius formulations found no equivalent claim. Closely related accessible papers and indexed records were compared by their assumptions and implications, not their titles. Historical-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Historical priority in specialized noncommuting quadratic-product inequalities not indexed by the searches remains uncertain.
A modern semidefinite-dual numerical-radius framework may imply the function after nontrivial specialization; no exact identical statement was identified.
Published-record semantic indexing is not an exhaustive novelty certification.

value.rationale: It solves a natural sharp, dimension-independent spectral-conditioning refinement of the universal positive-product numerical-radius inequality for the whole square-zero class, with an optimal constant determined by exactly two spectral numbers. The result characterizes extremizer existence and gives critical singular/nearly scalar expansions, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a routine restatement of the known unconditioned constant.
